description:
## Question

Given the research on its runtime and requirements, does the test-runner parity suite become a CI job (on every change? only when buck2-source.nix changes?) or stay a manual step in the bump checklist?

comments.text:
Resolution:
1. The parity suite stays a manual step in the pin-bump checklist; the CI gate is filed as its own ticket turnkey-kxe, outside this map. Why: bumps are rare, the suite takes about 3 min locally, a slim CI shell is a larger piece of work other checks could share, and Linux-only CI would miss macOS differences. jj doesn't run git hooks, so a pre-push hook can't enforce it either.
2. Evidence: the commit that bumps the pin must include the parity summary line (scenarios matched, target count, buck2 release, platform), so jj log shows the gate ran.

title: Should the parity suite be a CI gate for buck2 pin bumps?
